latest.summary: 19 submissions reviewed for the Central calendar day of Sunday 09/27/2026: four air job / OWL submissions, three H2S Equipment Rig Check job reports, three standalone H2S Equipment Rig Up Rig Check Photos Forms, three PB H2S Safety Supervision job reports, three H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Forms, two Traile

concerns.title: Alexander Clubb — SM Energy inspection route, Ensign 57, Midland, 09/27 06:32 PM. An H2S sensor read 200 ppm during the equipment check and put the location into full ala
concerns.text: : "Talked to dayshift cm and let him know I was gonna be going through all equipment on site, had issues getting the lights to go after, resorted to replacing the repeater on top of the doghouse and after and doing relay both LAA flashed, when grabbing the cellar sensor the sensor jumped up to 200 ppm and started running the alarms fully, after trying to recalibrate it and not being successful I replaced it with a stand I had with me, went through all other equipment and battery levels and functionality were in spec. Heading home." Follow-up: confirm the failed sensor and the replaced doghouse repeater were tagged out and returned, and confirm whether the 200 ppm indication was a true readin

concerns.title: Alexander Clubb — SM Energy inspection route, HP 628, Hobbs NM, 09/27 11:44 AM. A loud alarm was found unplugged on arrival. The technician's words
concerns.text: : "Talked to Jeff and let him know was here checking up on things, LAA on the housing was unplugged and I addressed the error sense someone unplugged it but let him know I moved my plug so it wouldn't trip the outlet, went up to run the lights and both LAA flashed, went through all equipment verifying battery levels and functionality, didn't find any errors or damage to any equipment." Follow-up: the alarm was restored on the spot, but a third party unplugging a loud alarm is worth raising with the customer so it does not recur.

concerns.title: Jordan Lemmons — Ovintiv, H&P 395 Terlingua, 09/27 07:35 AM, job 35099. Damaged and missing equipment found during the rig check
concerns.text: : "Comments or Concerns: Was missing a radio card and half the sensor had battery acid on them" The close-out adds: "Replaced battery on half the equipment because there was battery acid on them and recalibrated them and had to put a radio card in one because it was gone." "Loud Alarms and Lights Tested?: No"

8. Rolando Flores — Trailer Readiness Form, trailer 601, CSRHI Andrews Shop, 09/27 03:01 PM. Missing equipment reported on the trailer:

The same form answers "No" to "Does your trailer have a AV-3000 box?". Follow-up: the problem is named but no notified party is, so it is not clear anyone downstream has this. Confirm who was told and whether trailer 601 went to location without the AV-3000 kit.
Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

Four air job / OWL forms were filed today, all at XTO locations by Stefanie Kirschke and Rolando Flores. Only one carries any stop-work selection, and it is the routine one. No form selected "Unsafe conditions" and no form selected "Stop work authority utilized". This section is therefore short today.

"Stop work authority was discussed" — selected on one form: Stefanie Kirschke, XTO Morgan Owens 24E #5H, job 35097_1, 09/27 10:51 AM. This is the pre-job discussion item, not the exercise of stop-work authority. Her narrative describes a routine reconnect alongside a workover crew: "Did a reconnect while workover was still on site." Nothing on the form describes an unsafe condition arising. No action needed.

Neither stop-work option selected — the other three OWL forms: Rolando Flores at Morgan Owens 24E #5H (35097_2), Stefanie Kirschke at Brook N-13EM #213H (35102_1) and Rolando Flores at Brook N-13EM #213H (35102_2). None of them contains a narrative describing an unsafe condition either, so this is consistent rather than an inverse case.

One pattern worth the training point: the "What went well?" multi-select is byte-for-byte identical on all four forms, and Rolando Flores's "What did we observe?" selection and both of his continued narratives are identical across his two separate jobs. That is a selection being carried forward rather than made fresh for each job. It is not a safety finding, but it is the behaviour that makes these selections unreliable when one of them does matter.

The inverse case, reported as a real item: Jordan Lemmons found a missing radio card and battery acid on half a sensor set today, and Alexander Clubb found a loud alarm unplugged and a sensor alarming at 200 ppm. None of those reached a "What did we observe?" multi-select, because rig check and photo forms do not carry one — they surfaced only because both technicians wrote them into a free-text comments field. That is worth noting when judging how much the multi-select is actually telling you.

Neither Kirschke nor Flores appeared on the stop-work confirmation list on previous days. Nathan Contreras, Jose Campos and Michael Jobe, who did, are all on DAYS OFF or contingency rows today and filed nothing.
Missing required documentation

Both job boards for 09/27/2026 were available and were used. Seventeen manned rows were checked — twelve on the Permian Basin board and five on the ArkLaTex board — after excluding rows marked CANCELLED, ON STANDBY, DAYS OFF and WTX SUPPORT.

Both technicians filed their own job submission (35097_1 and 35097_2). Trailer 601 has its two Trailer Inspection Forms — Kirschke at 07:43 AM at the Andrews shop and Flores at 01:17 PM on location at Midkiff — and its one Trailer Readiness Form, Flores at 03:01 PM. This looks lopsided at a glance because Flores filed two of the three; that satisfies the requirement, which is counted across the crew assigned to the trailer and not one each. No follow-up needed

XTO Energy, Brook N-13EM #213H, air job, Kirschke and Flores, jobs 35102_1 and 35102_2 — both submissions filed, but this job does not appear anywhere on the 09/27 board. No documentation is missing; the gap is on the board side. Worth confirming it was added work rather than a board omission, and whether it used trailer 601 as well.

Benjamin Boutte 1099 (SM Energy, Junior Mint Federal 211H, AT# 151), Brynn Taylor 1099 (SM Energy flowback Junior Mint), Trevor McKenzie 1099 (Ovintiv H&P 379), Don Quisenberry 1099 (Comstock Danford CS 1H) and Marcos Morales 1099 (Mitsui Lipsey 1H) all hold night assignments on the 09/27 board. Those shifts run into 09/28 and their forms would normally land after midnight, so their absence at the time of this review says nothing. They will be picked up in tomorrow's review.

Rig checks and inspection routes — all covered. Jordan Lemmons filed both Ovintiv rig checks (H&P 395 and H&P 616), Brianda Sandoval filed the Ovintiv H&P 551 Fasken rig check, and Alexander Clubb filed three equipment photo forms covering his SM Energy inspection route (Ensign 57, HP 376, HP 628). All four of those board rows carry AT# N/A, so no trailer forms were required for them and no air-trailer fields were expected.
Field service — no field service jobs on either board for 09/27. Nothing to check.

One coverage question I cannot settle from the forms, flagged rather than asserted. Seven supervision rows across the two boards name a trailer in AT# — 272, 118, 141/175, 148 and 151 on the Permian board, 140 and 506 on the ArkLaTex board — and no Trailer Inspection Form or Trailer Readiness Form was received for any of those trailer numbers today. The only trailer forms filed were for 601, the air job trailer. It is not clear to me whether the two-inspections-plus-one-readiness requirement extends to trailers assigned to supervision rows, or whether it is satisfied by the air-trailer photo section and the hydro and cascade fields carried inside the H2S daily itself — Justin Pack's and Bobby Fleming's dailies do include those sections and they are complete. I have not counted these as missing forms. Please confirm which reading is correct and I will apply it from the next review onward.

Bobby Fleming, daily at Junior Mint Fed 211H: Bottle Hydro Dates "8/27x4 7/27x1 3/28x1", Pressure on Cascade System "6@3300" — complete.
Bobby Fleming, daily at Junior Mint Fed 222H: Bottle Hydro Dates "5/28x4 1/28x1", Pressure on Cascade System "5@1800" — complete.
Justin Pack, daily at Lipsey 1H: Bottle Hydro Dates "6@7/23", Pressure on Cascade System "6@2400" — complete.

Exempt because the board AT# is exactly "N/A": Ovintiv H&P 395, H&P 616 and H&P 551 rig checks, the SM Energy inspection route, and the Ovintiv H&P 379 supervision row. Blank air-trailer fields and absent trailer photo sections on those are expected.

Benjamin Boutte, a known repeat on blank hydro dates and cascade pressure, filed no form carrying those fields today — his submission is a job report with no daily inspection section — so there is nothing to compare against for 09/27.

Rolando Flores — Trailer Readiness Form, trailer 601: the Cascade Low Pressure Alarm photo and the AV-3000 Masks photo are both timestamped 10/25/2024 02:54 PM. He filed three inspection forms and found a 200 ppm sensor. One of those two rows is wrong.
Stefanie Kirschke is also on a DAYS OFF row on the same board while being listed on two Morgan Owens air job rows, and she worked and filed four submissions.

Brianda Sandoval's rig check similarly records "Equipment Issues Need Attention: None." while her comments describe replacing sensor batteries and having trouble calibrating three of them. Comments to management other than N/A
All five forms carrying a "Comments or Concerns for Management" field — both Trailer Inspection Forms and all three H2S dailies — read "N/A". Nothing was raised through that channel today.

Everything substantive came through the differently named "Comments or Concerns" field on the rig check and equipment photo forms: Clubb's three entries, Lemmons's two, and Sandoval's, all quoted above or in the safety section. It is worth noting that the field management actually watches was empty on every form that has it, while the real content sat in a field with a different name.
The Trailer Readiness Form equivalent, "Is anything wrong or missing?", carries "Av 3000 kit missing" with no notified party named.

clean.text: Justin Pack filed an H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form for Mitsui E&P / MEP at Lipsey 1H with nothing requiring attention — FR answered Yes, all four compliance questions Yes, hydro dates and cascade pressure complete, comments N/A, and every one of roughly eighty photos captured on 09/27. Brianda Sandoval's Ovintiv rig check at Fasken MD 9 U (job 35098) is clean on its face: loud alarms and lights tested Yes, work described in full, all photos from 09/27, with only the checklist-versus-comments wording noted above. Stefanie Kirschke's two air job submissions (35097_1 and 35102_1) carry complete OWL narratives including the Learn section, tube counts recorded and all photos from 09/27 — her FR answer is the separate finding above and does not touch these. Rolando Flores's Trailer Inspection Form for trailer 601 is clean: FR Yes, comments N/A, all eleven photos from 09/27.

Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph will not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so this review can confirm those photos were taken and when, but not what they show.

A second limitation applies specifically to tonight. This review ran at 11:00 PM Central, so the usual sweep of the following morning for late-arriving submissions could not be performed. Any form carrying a 09/27 form date that reaches the mailbox after midnight is not in this report. Given that five night-shift assignments were open on the 09/27 boards, some late arrivals are expected; they will be picked up and attributed to 09/27 in the next review.

19 of 19 submissions read. The job board was available — the 09/27/2026 boards emailed by Blake Walton at 09:20 AM Central were used, both the ArkLaTex and Permian Basin workbooks, sheet "9-27" in each. Seventeen manned board rows were checked for coverage: twelve on the Permian Basin board and five on the ArkLaTex board.
